description: Figure 5(a) is a line plot that illustrates the training loss curves for different methods during training from scratch. The x-axis, labeled "TFLOPs," represents the number of tera-floating-point operations, with a logarithmic scale ranging from $1e7$ to $9e8$. The y-axis, labeled "Loss Value," represents the training loss, with a linear scale from 94 to 100. The plot displays six distinct lines, each corresponding to a different method: Vanilla (purple, solid), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, dashed), SepLLM (n=128) (blue, dashed), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, dashed), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, dashed), and StrmLLM (n=256) (black, solid). The Vanilla method starts at a loss of approximately 97.5 and decreases to about 96.5. The SepLLM (n=64) method starts at a loss of approximately 97.5 and decreases to about 96.5. The SepLLM (n=128) method starts at a loss of approximately 97.5 and decreases to about 96.5. The SepLLM (n=64, H) method starts at a loss of approximately 97.5 and decreases to about 96.5. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) method starts at a loss of approximately 97.5 and decreases to about 96.5. The StrmLLM (n=256) method starts at a loss of approximately 97.5 and decreases to about 96.5. All methods show a general downward trend in loss as the number of TFLOPs increases.
